questions.question: Let A and B be two towers with the same base. From the mid point of the line joining their feet, the angles of elevation of the tops of A and B are 30° and 45°, respectively. The ratio of the heights of A and B is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46252fb6b1a6a695f2bc246d7728e73bbf391accd4f414eeb00415799d2354b1.png] 

A and B are two towers having the same base

The angle of elevation of tops of A and B from point c = 30 ° and 45 °

According to the question,

Midpoint to the line joining the feet bc = cd

Tan 30° ⇒frac{{height (ab)}}{{base(bc)}} = (1)/({sqrt 3 )} ---------------(i)

Tan 45° ⇒ frac{{height(de) }}{{base(cd)}} = 1 -----------------(ii)

From the equation (i) & (ii)

Bc = cd = de = sqrt 3 

⇒ ab : de = 1:sqrt 3 

**∴ The ratio of the heights of A : B ={bf{1}}:sqrt {bf{3}} **

questions.question: The length of the shadow of a vertical pole on the ground is 18 m. If the angle of elevation of the sun at that time is θ, such that cos theta = frac {12}{13}, then what is the height (in m) of the pole?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of shadow = 18 m

cos θ = 12/13

**Concept used:**

In a right angled triangle,

Cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

Let height of pole be h.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b7f9d27f1291a0c0898132bcd5337af2b5ae599b7834d6b20de29ffb3f00e175.png] 

In ΔABC,

cos θ = BC/AC = 12/13

Let BC and AC be 12x and 13x respectively.

12x = 18

⇒ x = 3/2

By pythagoras theorem,

(AC)² = (AB)² + (BC)²

⇒ (13x)2 = (h)2 + (12x)2

⇒ 169x² = (h)2 + 144x²

⇒ 169x2 - 144x2 = (h)2

⇒ 25x² = (h)2

⇒ h = 5x

⇒ h = 5 × (3/2)

⇒ h = 7.5 m

**∴ The height of the pole is 7.5 m**

questions.question: Height of a tower is 120 metres. The angle of elevation of the top of tower from a point B is 75°. Point B is on the ground level. What is the distance (in metres) of point B from the base of tower?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The relationship between Height (h) and Distance from base (d) is given by d = h × cot θ.

Given: h = 120 m and θ = 75°.

Standard value: cot 75° = tan 15° = 2 − √3.

Substituting the values: d = 120 × (2 − √3) m.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 (2 − √3) m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Height of tower (AC) = 120 m, Angle of elevation at point B = 75°.

Formula Used: tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e58cb9e5350d31e47c440ad2a9a07ca5489cb52604c17feb0052342dbda99532.png] 

⇒ tan 75° = 120 / BC

⇒ BC = 120 / tan 75°

⇒ tan 75° = tan(45° + 30°) = (tan 45° + tan 30°) / (1 − tan 45° × tan 30°)

⇒ tan 75° = (1 + 1/√3) / (1 − 1/√3) = (√3 + 1) / (√3 − 1) = 2 + √3

⇒ BC = 120 / (2 + √3)

⇒ BC = [120 / (2 + √3)] × [(2 − √3) / (2 − √3)]

⇒ BC = 120(2 − √3) / (4 − 3) = 120(2 − √3)

**∴ The correct answer is 120 (2 − √3) m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Values for 15° and 75°

tan 15° = cot 75° = 2 − √3 and tan 75° = cot 15° = 2 + √3.

Height and Distance Relation

For an angle of elevation θ, Distance = Height / tan θ. For θ = 45°, Height = Distance.

Rationalization Rule

To rationalize 1/(a + √b), multiply numerator and denominator by (a − √b) to use the identity (a+b)(a−b) = a² − b².</p

⇒ 1/√2 = BC/12

questions.question: Two poles of heights 10 m and 17 m are fixed to a level ground. The distance between the bottom of the poles is 24 m. What is the distance (in m) between their tops?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two poles of heights 10 m and 17 m are fixed to level ground.

The distance between the bottom of the poles is 24 m

**Concept used:**

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base² 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8600e18f3418fb31191fbbd34ca6ba010850980ac7cf11f6120156af2daf06b.png] 

Let AB be 10 m and CD be 17 m 

AP = BD = 24 m

AB = PD = 10 m

So, CP = 7 m

Applying pythagoras theorem in ΔACP

AC² = AP² + CP²

⇒ AC2 = 242 + 72

⇒ AC2 = 576 + 49

⇒ AC2 = 625

⇒ AC = 25

**∴ The distance (in m) between their tops is 25.**

questions.question: What is the angle of elevation of the sun when the shadow of a 9-m high pole is 3sqrt 3 m long?
questions.solution:
Given data:

Length of pole = 9 m

Length of shadow of the pole = 3√3 m

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/755161200461042ee6100874542431d0e0cb72b064dcfe78f335488dba4f612d.png] 

In the right-angled triangle ABC

tan θ = AC / BC

⇒ tan θ = 9 / 3√3

⇒ tan θ = √3

∴ θ = 60º

∴ The angle of the elevation of the sun is 60º.

questions.question: A vertical pole and a vertical tower are on the same level of ground in such a way that from the top of the pole, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60º and the angle of depression of the bottom of the tower is 30º. If the height of the tower is 76 m, then find the height (in m) of the pole.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the top of the pole = 60º

The angle of depression of the bottom of the tower from the top of the pole = 30º

**Calculation:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfb0c2544a2bad663ee4e25a4d647add56b66beaf0b065aece991286147b366f.png] **

Let, the height of the pole (AB) = CD = x m

So, the height of ED = (76 - x) m

So, In ΔACD, tan 30° = CD/AD

⇒ 1/√3 = x/AD

⇒ AD = √3x .....(1)

In ΔAED, tan 60° = ED/AD

⇒ √3 = (76 - x)/√3x

⇒ 76 - x = 3x

⇒ 3x + x = 76

⇒ 4x = 76

⇒ x = 76/4 = 19

**∴ The height (in m) of the pole is 19 m**
